subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Superposition: One Source at a Time
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Superposition: One Source at a Time.

hook.text: A circuit has three voltage sources. Solving them all at once is a headache.

buildup.text: Superposition says: turn off all sources but one and solve. Repeat for each source.

discovery.text: Add the individual answers together. The sum is the total response.

twist.text: Turning off a voltage source means replacing it with a wire. A current source becomes open.

climax.text: Superposition only works in linear circuits — no diodes or transistors allowed.

punchline.text: Solve one source at a time and add the results. Done.

quiz.question: What does 'turning off' a voltage source mean in superposition?
options: Setting it to its maximum value
Replacing it with a short circuit (wire)
Removing it and leaving the circuit open
